Code has been implemented that creates a dedicated NCCL communicator group used exclusively for KV cache migration, separate from the NCCL communicator group used for pipeline-parallel intermediate-state forwarding.

verification.spec: Inspect the code that initializes NCCL communicator groups and confirm two distinct ncclCommInitRank/ProcessGroup NCCL groups are created: one for pipeline-parallel intermediate-state forwarding and a separate one dedicated to KV cache migration. Verify migration send/recv paths use only the migration group's communicator handle.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that assigns a lower CUDA stream priority to the KV migration NCCL communicator group so that its GPU work yields to inference kernels on the inference stream.

verification.spec: Inspect the migration NCCL group's CUDA stream setup. Confirm the KV-migration stream is created with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority (or equivalent torch API) using a lower priority than the inference stream, and that migration NCCL ops are launched on that stream.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that spawns, for each participating GPU pair (r_s, r_d), a dedicated sender thread on r_s and receiver thread on r_d that extract/apply KV entries for the migrating layers, supporting multiple concurrent sender-receiver pairs within a single migrator.

verification.spec: Trigger a reconfiguration involving multiple (r_s, r_d) GPU pairs and inspect running threads (or log output) to confirm each pair spawns a dedicated sender thread on r_s and receiver thread on r_d handling that pair's migrating layers, and that multiple pairs can be active concurrently.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that transfers KV cache blocks over the dedicated migration NCCL group using ncclSend/ncclRecv operations, transferring data directly between GPU memories on the two nodes over InfiniBand.

verification.spec: Trigger a PP reconfiguration between the two testbed GPUs and confirm via NCCL debug logs (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) or code inspection that KV cache blocks are transferred using ncclSend/ncclRecv on the dedicated migration communicator, with source/destination pointers residing on GPU memory.

sub_tasks.requirements: The two-phase handshake protocol with asymmetric entry semantics that serializes NCCL operations across inference and migration communicator groups to avoid circular waits has been implemented.
Code has been implemented that maintains a per-GPU mutex serializing all NCCL operations issued from that GPU across both the inference and KV-migration communicator groups.

verification.spec: Inspect NCCL issuing paths in the worker code and confirm a per-GPU mutex (e.g., std::mutex, threading.Lock) guards all NCCL send/recv calls issued from that worker across both the inference and migration groups.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that pipeline-parallel intermediate-state (inference) NCCL send/recv operations proceed immediately after acquiring the per-GPU mutex, without any additional handshake, so that the inference data path is prioritized.

verification.spec: Inspect the inference-path NCCL send/recv wrapper and confirm it acquires only the per-GPU mutex before issuing the NCCL op, with no ACK/ACCEPT/REJECT TCP handshake in that code path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the migration sender that, before issuing an ncclSend on the migration group, first acquires the local per-GPU mutex and then sends an ACK message to the receiver over an out-of-band TCP channel.

verification.spec: Inspect the migration sender code path and confirm the sequence: (1) acquire the per-GPU mutex, (2) send an ACK message to the receiver over a TCP socket (out-of-band from NCCL) before issuing ncclSend.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the migration receiver that, upon receiving an ACK, attempts to acquire its local per-GPU mutex and responds with ACCEPT on success or REJECT on failure over the same TCP channel.

verification.spec: Inspect the migration receiver code and confirm that upon receiving an ACK it attempts try_lock (or non-blocking acquire) on its per-GPU mutex; on success it sends ACCEPT over the same TCP channel, and on failure it sends REJECT.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that on receiving REJECT the sender releases its per-GPU mutex and retries the handshake after a timeout tau, while on ACCEPT both parties hold their local mutexes and proceed to issue the paired ncclSend/ncclRecv KV migration operations.

verification.spec: Force a REJECT scenario (e.g., have the receiver hold its mutex before ACK arrives) and verify the sender releases its mutex and retries after a configurable timeout tau. Then have the receiver release the mutex and confirm on ACCEPT both parties hold their local mutexes and paired ncclSend/ncclRecv KV migration ops execute.

sub_tasks.requirements: The two-phase handshake is applied only to KV migration NCCL operations and not to inference NCCL operations, so that inference NCCL send/recv issue paths do not include ACK/ACCEPT/REJECT exchange.

verification.spec: Confirm by code inspection that the two-phase ACK/ACCEPT/REJECT handshake logic is invoked only from the KV migration send/recv wrappers, and not from the inference PP intermediate-state send/recv wrappers.

sub_tasks.requirements: In a deadlock-inducing scenario reproducing Figure 7 (concurrent PP intermediate-state forwarding between GPU1 and GPU2 and KV migration from GPU2 to GPU1), the system with the two-phase handshake enabled completes both operations without hanging, whereas disabling the handshake reproduces the deadlock (operations do not complete within a timeout).

verification.spec: Reproduce the scenario in Figure 7 with GPU1<->GPU2 doing concurrent PP intermediate-state forwarding and GPU2->GPU1 KV migration. With the two-phase handshake enabled, verify both operations complete within a bounded time. Then disable the handshake and confirm the setup hangs (times out), reproducing the deadlock.

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV patching mechanism used by the KV Migrator to stream incremental KV updates and drive convergence tracking has been integrated into the migrator.

Code has been implemented for the sender thread's drain-and-transmit loop that periodically atomically extracts the dirty slot set D from the per-migration dirty bitmap, resets the bitmap to zero, gathers KV data at those slots from GPU memory, and transmits the resulting KV patch over the migration NCCL group.

verification.spec: Inspect the sender thread's main loop and confirm it periodically: atomically extracts D = {s : B[s]=1} from the per-migration dirty bitmap, zeros the bitmap, gathers KV entries at slots in D from GPU memory, and sends the resulting patch via the migration NCCL group. Instrument counters to verify multiple drain-and-transmit cycles occur during a migration.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the receiver thread that continuously receives incoming KV patches and writes them into the local layer KV cache at the corresponding slot indices for the migrating layers.

verification.spec: Inspect the receiver thread's loop and confirm it repeatedly receives KV patches (slot indices + KV data) from the migration NCCL group and writes each patch's entries to the correct slot indices in the local layer KV cache. Run a small migration and check post-migration KV cache values at destination match sent values.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that maintains, per receiver thread, a cumulative counter T_applied incremented upon applying each incoming KV patch and exposes T_applied to the Reconfiguration Coordinator via a Collective::GetLastSyncedTokenIndex RPC.

verification.spec: Verify each receiver thread maintains a T_applied counter incremented per applied patch. From the Reconfiguration Coordinator, invoke Collective::GetLastSyncedTokenIndex RPC during migration and confirm it returns the per-GPU T_applied values, monotonically increasing over time.

sub_tasks.requirements: The convergence threshold tau used by the migrator/coordinator to trigger the final cutover is configurable and defaults to 50 tokens on the InfiniBand ~100 Gbps testbed.

verification.spec: Inspect the coordinator/migrator config for the convergence threshold tau. Confirm it is user-configurable (CLI flag, config file, or constructor argument) and defaults to 50 tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measurable behavioral properties of the KV Migrator during live reconfiguration have been verified.

With the KV migration NCCL group running concurrently with inference NCCL, ongoing inference is not blocked by KV migration: measured inference TPOT during background KV transfer remains within a small tolerance of TPOT without migration (i.e., migration does not stall the inference stream due to CUDA stream priority isolation).

verification.spec: Measure per-token latency (TPOT) during inference under two conditions on the A100+L40S testbed: (a) no ongoing KV migration, (b) with background KV migration NCCL transfers actively running. Confirm TPOT in (b) is within a small tolerance (e.g., <20%) of (a), demonstrating migration does not stall the inference stream.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under the pattern-shifting benchmark workload on LLaMA-70B (A100 + L40S testbed), the full PipeLive KV Migrator (asynchronous weight loading + KV patch enabled) achieves a stop time of approximately 10 ms across migration sizes of 4, 8, 12, and 16 migrated layers, as reported in Figure 13 [claim 17].

verification.spec: Run the pattern-shifting benchmark workload on LLaMA-70B on A100+L40S with full PipeLive (async weight loading + KV patch enabled). Trigger reconfigurations with 4, 8, 12, and 16 migrated layers and measure stop time (duration of the synchronized cutover window). Confirm each is approximately 10 ms.

sub_tasks.requirements: Compared to disabling KV patching (stop-and-copy variant), the full PipeLive migrator reduces the reconfiguration stop time from seconds down to on the order of 10 ms on the LLaMA-70B pattern-shifting benchmark, matching the paper's abstract/conclusion claim [claim 18].

verification.spec: Run the pattern-shifting benchmark on LLaMA-3 70B (A100+L40S testbed) and trigger a PP reconfiguration. Measure stop time (duration during which inference is paused for final KV sync + commit) with full PipeLive vs. KV-patch-disabled variant. Assert PipeLive stop time <= ~15 ms while KV-patch-disabled stop time is on the order of seconds (>=1000 ms).

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV patch drain-and-transmit cycle causes total migration time to increase modestly relative to the stop-and-copy baseline (KV patch disabled) as the number of migrated layers grows from 4 to 16, consistent with the trend shown in Figure 13.

verification.spec: Trigger PP reconfigurations that migrate {4, 8, 12, 16} layers under the pattern-shifting benchmark with and without KV patch. Record total migration wall-clock time for each configuration. Assert that KV-patch-enabled total migration time is greater than or equal to KV-patch-disabled at each migration size, and that both increase monotonically with migrated layer count, matching Figure 13's trend.

sub_tasks.requirements: The incremental KV patching mechanism (dirty bitmap per sender, drain-and-transmit cycles, convergence tracking via T_sched vs T_applied with threshold τ=50 tokens) has been correctly implemented.

Code has been implemented that instantiates one dirty bitmap B^(i_s, i_d) per sender thread for each (source GPU, destination GPU) pair involved in KV migration, sized to the total number of physical KV cache slots N of the migrating layers.

verification.spec: Inspect the KV migrator sender-thread class. Verify that when a migration session for (i_s, i_d) is created, a dirty-bitmap data structure is instantiated per (source, destination) pair, whose length equals the total number of physical KV slots N for the layers being migrated.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that initializes the dirty bitmap to all zeros at the start of a KV migration session.

verification.spec: Construct a fresh KV migrator sender for a small mock layer set. Immediately after initialization and before any inference step, read the dirty bitmap and assert every entry equals 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that after each inference step, the inference worker marks slots written during that step (set S^(t)) as dirty by setting B[s]=1 for all s in S^(t) for layers currently under migration.

verification.spec: Start a migration for a layer under active inference. Simulate/execute an inference step that writes to a known set of KV slots S. After the step returns, inspect the dirty bitmap and assert B[s]=1 for every s in S and B[s]=0 for slots not written.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dirty bitmap update path uses atomic or lock-protected operations so that concurrent marking by the inference worker and draining by the sender thread does not lose or corrupt dirty entries.

verification.spec: Run a stress test where an inference thread continuously marks random slots dirty while the sender thread continuously drains. After N iterations, verify (a) union of all drained sets equals the set of all marked slots (no losses), and (b) no exception/race is raised. Inspect source to confirm the bitmap read/write path uses atomics or a lock.

sub_tasks.requirements: The drain-and-transmit cycle on the sender and the corresponding receiver-apply loop have been implemented.
Code has been implemented that periodically drains the dirty bitmap on the sender by atomically extracting the dirty set D = {s : B[s] = 1} and resetting B to zero in a single logical step.

verification.spec: Pre-populate the dirty bitmap with a known set D of set bits. Invoke the sender's drain method. Assert (a) it returns exactly D, and (b) immediately after the call the entire bitmap reads as zero, and (c) the extract+reset happens atomically (i.e., concurrent marker never sees a partially-cleared bitmap in a state that would drop its bit).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that gathers the KV data corresponding to the physical slot indices in D from GPU memory into a contiguous KV patch buffer for transmission.

Assert the resulting patch buffer is contiguous, has length |D| * per-slot-size, and contains bit-exact copies of the values at indices D in the expected order.

sub_tasks.requirements: The sender thread transmits the KV patch (indices and data) to destination GPU i_d over the dedicated lower-priority NCCL migration communicator group.

verification.spec: Inspect the sender transmit call site. Verify it uses the NCCL communicator handle associated with the dedicated migration group (not the pipeline-parallel inference group) and that this migration group is created with a lower CUDA stream priority than the inference stream.

sub_tasks.requirements: The drain-and-transmit cycle repeats on a best-effort loop until the coordinator signals migration commit; a subsequent cycle only starts after the previous transmission completes.

verification.spec: Start a migration and monitor the sender thread. Verify (a) drain-transmit cycles repeat continuously until a commit signal from the coordinator, (b) after the signal the loop terminates, and (c) instrumentation shows cycle N+1 begins only after cycle N's transmit future/handle completes (no overlapping outstanding transmissions from the same sender).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented on the receiver side where each receiver thread continuously receives incoming KV patches and writes their contents into the corresponding local layer KV cache slots.

verification.spec: Post a synthetic KV patch (indices + data) into the receiver's NCCL channel. Verify the receiver thread wakes, receives it, and writes each token's KV values into the correct local layer/slot addresses; then post another patch and confirm continuous receive-loop behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: Multiple sender-receiver thread pairs can coexist within a single KV migrator to handle concurrent migrations across different (i_s, i_d) GPU pairs.

Start migration and assert that two sender threads (and two receiver threads) exist concurrently and both make progress in parallel.

The scheduler maintains a cumulative token counter T_sched that is incremented by n^(t) = |S^(t)| after each inference step, and exposes it via getLastScheduledTokenIndex().
